metadata.scenario_context: Mike, Kim, and Emily, who are university students and schoolmates, have recently partnered to start a company that has just secured a significant investment. They are preparing to celebrate. Recent news indicates that the government is introducing new policies to assist businesses, which they are planning to discuss.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Romania have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss going to a barbecue buffet.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking... maybe we should celebrate our investment with a barbecue buffet? It sounds like a fun way to unwind and enjoy some good food together. What do you think? 

Also, have you seen the news about the new government policies for businesses? I feel like there's a lot of confidence in the press about it. Don't you agree?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: A barbecue buffet sounds fine. We can definitely enjoy some good food together. But about the press... I have to say, I have no confidence in it at all. They have a tendency to twist stories in ways that aren't reliable. That's just how it is in Romania. What else do you have in mind for the celebration?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I'm glad you think the barbecue buffet sounds fine! We should definitely go for it. But I really don’t understand your lack of confidence in the press. In China, we have a great deal of trust in the media; they play a vital role in informing us. Anyway, what do you think about inviting Emily too? It could be more fun with the three of us.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Inviting Emily sounds good; the more, the merrier. But back to the press—trust is different across cultures. In Romania, it’s really tricky, and many just don’t rely on it for accurate information. I think that skepticism is warranted. So, barbecue buffet with Emily—let's make it happen! Any other ideas for the celebration?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Great! I'm excited for the barbecue buffet with Emily. I just really think that in China, we have a solid foundation of trust in the press, and it helps us stay informed. But... back to the celebration! How about we also plan some games or activities at the barbecue? It could make the day even more enjoyable! What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: Games and activities at the barbecue sound like a lot of fun. I'm all for it. But I still believe that relying on the press too much can lead to misinformation, especially from a Romanian perspective. Anyway, let's focus on making our celebration great. What kind of games do you have in mind?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I'm glad you're on board with the games and activities! For the barbecue, we could have some classic outdoor games like frisbee or volleyball. They’re always fun and get everyone involved. But I still don’t get the skepticism about the press. It’s so important to have reliable information, right? Let’s just make sure we have a great time at the BBQ! Do you have any favorite games you want to bring?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message: I don't know about that. I think at the end of the day, it's all the same. People figure it out, and as long as we're speaking the same language, there’s no need to overthink it. So, about the barbecue, I like the idea of frisbee and volleyball. Those games will definitely keep the energy up. What else do you think we should add?
shared_prefix.label: Denial
